data.gender_notes: Suren is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The Armenian name Suren is derived from the Old Persian word 'sur', meaning 'ruler' or 'lord'. In Armenian history, the name was borne by several kings and princes, including Suren I (r. 330–345 AD), who is considered the founder of the Armenian kingdom of Artsrunik. Suren is also the name of a saint in the Armenian Apostolic Church, commemorated on May 23.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for those who are called to rule and lead with wisdom and strength.
data.etymology: Suren belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ruler, Lord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Suren total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

Historically, Suren has been used among Caucasian Christians, reflecting its cultural and spiritual significance.

data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Suren is derived from the Persian word "sure" meaning rock or foundation. In Christian tradition, the name Suren signifies a strong foundation in faith and unwavering commitment to God. It symbolizes the rock-solid belief that God is the bedrock of one's life.

historical_references.reference: The Syrian prince Suren I, also known as Shapur, converted to Christianity in the early 4th century AD and ruled the Kingdom of Osroene from 331 to 344 AD.
historical_references.context: Kingdom of Osroene, located in present-day Turkey and Syria, was an important Christian state during the Roman period. Prince Suren I, who came to power after the Roman emperor Constantine's recognition of Christianity, adopted the Christian faith and ruled as a Christian king.

historical_references.reference: Suren II, also known as Shapur, was the last independent ruler of the Kingdom of Armenia from 320 to 367 AD. He embraced Christianity around 325 AD during a visit to Constantinople.
historical_references.context: The Kingdom of Armenia, located in present-day Armenia and eastern Turkey, was one of the first Christian states. Suren II, who came to power after a period of political instability, converted to Christianity during a visit to Constantinople, thus solidifying the Christian faith in the kingdom.
